excluded_note: These are SCOPE decisions about this project, not judgements about the documents or their publisher. Everything listed here is a real resource that helps somebody; it is simply not what this shelf carries. The shelf holds capabilities a reader keeps. It carries no policy asks, no pledges and no campaign activity — from any source, including ours. Recorded rather than silently dropped so the sorting is auditable and reversible.
framing_note: framing_flag marks an entry whose CONTENTS name a party, a figure or a contested position, even where its title and format are a capability. Flagged entries are held out of the shipped shelf until framing_cleared is true — not deleted, and not a judgement on the document. The page's welcome is explicitly cross-partisan, so serving these by default would contradict it before anyone had read a word. Clearing one is a one-word edit and Bill's call. Found by reading the guides on 2026-09-21; the listing page showed none of it.

own_howtos.note: Writing our own how-tos is IN SCOPE (Bill, 2026-09-21). The pivot said the app stops inventing solutions and guides people through other people's material — this does not reverse that. Attending a town meeting is not our idea. The distinction is between inventing a solution and writing a neutral how-to for a mechanic that already exists, where nobody publishes one without a side attached. Three candidates, all held items whose structure we want and whose framing we cannot use: what your town decides and when it meets; how to run an empty-chair town hall; a registration and voting-rights checklist.

library.name: The Unhacking Democracy shelf
library.rule: Does this teach a capability you keep?
library.rule_long: Knowing how to check a claim is yours afterwards. Signing a pledge, joining a campaign or backing a particular bill may all be worth doing — they are just not what this shelf is for, and we leave them off whoever they come from, ourselves included.
